sdk_dotnet_crud_code:
await axon.CreateAsync("person", new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["name"] = "Ana" });
await axon.DeleteAsync("person:ana");
sdk_rust_intro: The Rust client uses Tokio and returns Result.
sdk_rust_connection_desc: Connect with AxonOptions and select the context.
sdk_rust_signin_desc: signin and authenticate act on the connection.
sdk_rust_query_desc: query receives the statement and optional variables.
sdk_rust_query_code: let rows = axon.query("SELECT * FROM person", None).await?;
sdk_php_intro: WebSocket JSON-RPC client for PHP 8.1 and later.
sdk_php_connection_desc: connect opens the WebSocket connection. use selects its namespace and database, signin returns and stores a token, and authenticate accepts either that token or one obtained elsewhere.
sdk_php_query_desc: query executes AxonQL. Pass an associative array as the optional second argument to bind AxonQL variables by name.
sdk_php_crud_desc: The helpers return decoded JSON results. select and delete accept an optional filter as their second argument; create, update, and upsert accept a table or record target, while insert accepts a table.
sdk_php_session_desc: ping returns a boolean, version returns the server version, namespace and database expose the selected scope, and hello exposes the first server frame. Always close the transport when finished.
sdk_php_errors_desc: All SDK errors extend AxonBase\Error. RPC error codes are mapped to AuthError, ConflictError, NotLeaderError, NoQuorumError, RateLimitError, and ProtocolMismatchError. NotLeaderError also exposes leader and leaderAddress; ProtocolMismatchError exposes protocol and serverVersion.
sdk_php_migration_desc: Migrator loads one .axql file or all .axql files in a directory in lexical order. Migration exposes version, name, path, checksum, and sql. ensureTable creates the _migration tracking table; applied returns its version-to-checksum map; status marks each loaded migration as applied. up runs pending migrations once, records their SHA-256 checksum, and fails when an applied file changes. onBefore and onAfter run around every pending migration.
sdk_ruby_intro: WebSocket JSON-RPC client for Ruby and Rails applications.
sdk_ruby_connection_desc: Client.connect opens the WebSocket connection. use selects its namespace and database, signin returns and stores a token, and authenticate accepts either that token or one obtained elsewhere.
sdk_ruby_connection_code:
require "axonbase"

axon = AxonBase::Client.connect("ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws")
axon.use("test", "dev")
token = axon.signin("root", "root")
axon.authenticate(token)
sdk_ruby_query_desc: query executes AxonQL. Pass a Hash as the optional second argument to bind AxonQL variables by name.
sdk_ruby_crud_desc: The helpers return decoded JSON results. select and delete accept an optional filter as their second argument; create, update, and upsert accept a table or record target, while insert accepts a table.
sdk_ruby_crud_code:
created = axon.create("person", { "name" => "Ana", "age" => 30 })
selected = axon.select("person", "age >= 18")
inserted = axon.insert("person", { "name" => "Bia" })
updated = axon.update("person:ana", { "age" => 31 })
upserted = axon.upsert("person:bia", { "name" => "Bia", "age" => 28 })
deleted = axon.delete("person", "age < 18")
sdk_ruby_session_desc: ping returns a decoded result, version returns the server version, and the namespace, database, and hello readers expose connection state. Always close the transport when finished.
sdk_ruby_session_code:
alive = axon.ping
server_version = axon.version
namespace = axon.namespace
database = axon.database
hello = axon.hello
axon.close
sdk_ruby_errors_desc: All SDK errors inherit from AxonBase::Error. RPC error codes are mapped to AuthError, ConflictError, NotLeaderError, NoQuorumError, RateLimitError, and ProtocolMismatchError. NotLeaderError exposes leader and leader_address; ProtocolMismatchError exposes protocol and server_version.
sdk_ruby_errors_code:
begin
  axon.create("person", { "name" => "Ana" })
rescue AxonBase::NotLeaderError => error
  leader = error.leader_address
rescue AxonBase::AuthError
  # Sign in again or provide a valid token.
rescue AxonBase::Error => error
  code = error.code
end
sdk_ruby_migration_desc: Migrator loads one .axql file or all .axql files in a directory in lexical order. Migration exposes version, name, path, checksum, and sql. ensure_table creates the _migration tracking table; applied returns its version-to-checksum map; status marks each loaded migration as applied. up runs pending migrations once, records their SHA-256 checksum, and fails when an applied file changes. on_before and on_after run around every pending migration.
sdk_ruby_migration_code:
migrator = AxonBase::Migrator.new(axon)
migrator.on_before { |migration| Rails.logger.info("Applying #{migration.name}") }
migrator.on_after { |migration| Rails.logger.info("Applied #{migration.name}") }

migrator.ensure_table
migrations = migrator.load(Rails.root.join("db/axonbase_migrations").to_s)
checksums = migrator.applied
status = migrator.status(Rails.root.join("db/axonbase_migrations").to_s)
applied = migrator.up(Rails.root.join("db/axonbase_migrations").to_s)
again = migrator.up(Rails.root.join("db/axonbase_migrations").to_s) # [] when unchanged
getting_started_architecture_desc: A local session has three boundaries: the repository initiator, the server process, and the client transport.

getting_started_architecture.title: Docker Image
getting_started_architecture.desc: The official axonbase/axonbase:latest image runs the server with RocksDB as the default storage backend. It exposes port 8000 for HTTP and WebSocket.

getting_started_architecture.title: Storage
getting_started_architecture.desc: By default, RocksDB persists data in /data inside the container. Mount a volume to preserve data across restarts. Use AXON_PATH=memory for ephemeral testing.

getting_started_architecture.title: Request Scope
getting_started_architecture.desc: On HTTP /sql, Axon-Ns and Axon-Db headers select the namespace and database. A WebSocket JSON-RPC connection maintains selected scope, authentication, transactions, and live queries.

getting_started_prerequisites: Docker is required to run the axonbase/axonbase:latest image.
curl is used below as an HTTP client to interact with the server.
Use AXON_REQUIRE_AUTH=false only for local development. Keep authentication active on shared or deployed servers.
getting_started_session_desc: Run the commands in order while the server stays active. The two curl calls are independent HTTP requests, so they repeat the namespace and database headers.
cli_lifecycle_desc: The CLI is a WebSocket client, not the server launcher. A command opens /rpc/ws, receives a hello frame, selects scope when needed, executes the operation, prints a result, and closes the connection.
cli_lifecycle: First compile the project with Maven.
Use a WebSocket URL like ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws.
For sql, pass --ns and --db to send use before the AxonQL statement.
export and import always select the namespace and database passed as positional arguments.
cli_commands_desc: The entry point recognizes sql, repl, export, and import.
cli_workflows_desc: Examples use an in-memory server without authentication for local work.

cli_workflows.title: Execute a Statement with Scope
cli_workflows.desc: Pass the statement after the URL and optional scope flags.
cli_workflows.code:
axon sql ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws 'CREATE person CONTENT {name: "Ana"}' --ns test --db dev
axon sql ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws 'SELECT * FROM person' --ns test --db dev

cli_workflows.title: Explore Interactively
cli_workflows.desc: Open the REPL, see internal help with ?, select a scope, and type AxonQL.
cli_workflows.code:
axon repl
axon> use test dev
axon> SELECT * FROM person
axon> exit

cli_workflows.title: Export and Restore a Scope
cli_workflows.desc: export prints the result of SELECT * FROM __export.
cli_workflows.code:
axon export ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws test dev > backup.dump
axon import ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws test dev backup.dump

cli_workflows.title: About --vars
cli_workflows.desc: The sql command accepts --vars JSON and interprets its value.
cli_workflows.code:
# Interpreted but not sent by the current CLI implementation:
axon sql ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws 'RETURN $name' --vars '{"name":"Ana"}'

sdk_overview_jdbc_desc: axonbase-jdbc is a Java integration adapter over the AxonBase WebSocket JSON-RPC SDK. It implements a JDBC subset via Connection, Statement, PreparedStatement, and ResultSet.
sdk_parity_desc: All eight connectors share the same core AxonBase capabilities: connection, query, transactions, live events, KV, certificates, migrations, and sagas.
search_overview_subtitle: AxonBase replaces Elasticsearch for BM25 full-text search, Qdrant or Pinecone for HNSW vector search, dedicated geo services like MongoDB Geo or Elastic Geo, graph databases like Neo4j or Dgraph, and analytical column stores like ClickHouse, all within a single database with native SQL.
search_overview_diagram_alt: Diagram of AxonBase's five search engines: BM25 full-text, HNSW vector, geo radius, graph traversal, and columnar index
search_overview_replace_desc: Most architectures combine Elasticsearch for text search, Qdrant or Pinecone for vector similarity, MongoDB Geo or Elastic Geo for location queries, Neo4j or Dgraph for graph traversal, and ClickHouse for analytical aggregation. AxonBase eliminates all these external dependencies with native SQL engines implementing BM25, HNSW, GEO, graph traversal, and columnar index, reducing infrastructure complexity and operational cost.
search_overview_ft_desc: Industry-standard BM25 ranking with tokenization, stopword removal, and stemming via CREATE ANALYZER and CREATE INDEX SEARCH.
search_overview_vector_desc: Hierarchical Navigable Small World index for approximate nearest neighbor search. Configure DIMENSION and DIST per index.
search_overview_geo_desc: Geohash grid spatial index on GeoJSON points: a radius or polygon query reads only the grid cells around it, with real-time distance in meters.
search_overview_graph_desc: Directed adjacency edges with RELATE and single-line AxonQL traversal for friend-of-friend and path queries.
search_overview_columnar_desc: Columnar index that answers count, sum, avg, min, and max (with GROUP BY and WHERE) from the index entries alone, without loading documents, when every column of the query has a COLUMNAR index. EXPLAIN shows COLUMNAR_AGG; otherwise the documents are read.
search_ft_subtitle: Replace Elasticsearch: native BM25 text search with analysis pipelines, inverted indexes, and ranked results, all in SQL.
search_ft_scenario_desc: A content management system stores thousands of articles and needs to search by title and body with relevance ranking. AxonBase replaces a separate Elasticsearch cluster with a native BM25 search engine.
search_ft_bm25_desc: BM25 (Best Matching 25) is the industry-standard ranking function used by Elasticsearch and Lucene. It scores documents by term frequency (how many times a term appears in the document), inverse document frequency (how rare the term is in the corpus), and field-length normalization (shorter fields are more significant). AxonBase implements BM25 natively with configurable k1 and b parameters.
search_ft_index_desc: Define an analyzer with tokenization, stopword filtering, and stemming rules, then create a search index on the relevant columns. The analyzer processes text identically during indexing and querying.
search_ft_index_code:
CREATE ANALYZER my_analyzer
  WITH tokenizer = 'standard',
       filters  = ['lowercase', 'stopwords', 'stemmer'];

CREATE INDEX SEARCH articles_idx
  ON TABLE articles
  WITH analyzer = my_analyzer,
       COLUMNS  = (title, body);
search_ft_query_desc: Use the double @@ operator to activate text search. The search::score() function returns the BM25 relevance score, which you can use in ORDER BY and WHERE.
search_ft_query_code: SELECT id, title, search::score() AS relevance FROM articles WHERE body @@ 'machine learning' ORDER BY relevance DESC LIMIT 20;
search_ft_docker_desc: Exemplo completo de Docker Compose com tabela de artigos, analisador, indice de busca e dados de amostra.
search_ft_docker_code:
version: '3.8'
services:
  axonbase:
    image: axonbase/axonbase:latest
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      AXONBASE_PASSWORD: mypassword

  setup:
    image: axonbase/axonbase:latest
    depends_on: [ axonbase ]
    entrypoint:
      - axonbase
      - -c
      - |
        CREATE TABLE artigos (
          id    SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
          titulo TEXT NOT NULL,
          corpo  TEXT NOT NULL
        );

        CREATE ANALYZER meu_analisador
          WITH tokenizer = 'standard',
               filters  = ['lowercase', 'stopwords', 'stemmer'];

        CREATE INDEX SEARCH artigos_idx
          ON TABLE artigos
          WITH analyzer = meu_analisador,
               COLUMNS  = (titulo, corpo);

        INSERT INTO artigos (titulo, corpo) VALUES
          ('Intro a ML', 'Machine learning esta transformando industrias'),
          ('Deep Learning', 'Redes neurais e avancos em aprendizado profundo');
search_vector_subtitle: Replace Qdrant and Pinecone: native HNSW nearest neighbor search with configurable dimensions and distance functions.
search_vector_scenario_desc: An AI agent built with LangChain embeds product descriptions into 384-dimensional vectors. When a user asks about similar items, the agent needs semantic search across millions of embeddings. AxonBase replaces a dedicated vector database with a native HNSW index.
search_vector_hnsw_desc: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) builds a multi-layer graph where each layer is a downsampled version of the layer below. Search starts at the top layer and descends to finer granularity, achieving approximate nearest neighbor search in O(log n) time.
search_vector_index_code: CREATE INDEX knowledge_embedding ON TABLE knowledge_chunks COLUMNS embedding HNSW DIMENSION 384 DIST cos;
search_vector_query_desc: Use vector::similarity::cosine() para calcular a distancia semantica entre uma coluna de embedding e um vetor de consulta. Ordene por pontuacao e limite aos vizinhos mais proximos.
search_vector_query_code: SELECT id, content, vector::distance::cosine(embedding, [0.11, 0.44, 0.76, 0.35]) AS distance FROM knowledge_chunks ORDER BY distance ASC LIMIT 5;
search_vector_hybrid_desc: Combine BM25 filtering with vector similarity ranking in a single query. WHERE filters candidates by full-text, while ORDER BY ranks by vector distance.
search_vector_hybrid_code: SELECT id, content, vector::distance::cosine(embedding, [0.11, 0.44, 0.76, 0.35]) AS distance FROM knowledge_chunks WHERE content @@ "vector search" ORDER BY distance ASC LIMIT 5;
search_vector_roadmap_title: Planejado: pipeline de PDFs do S3 para busca vetorial
search_vector_roadmap_desc: Este fluxo e uma proposta futura e nao esta disponivel. O codigo S3 atual do AxonBase executa backup e restauracao de snapshots; ele nao descobre objetos para ingestao nem extrai texto de PDFs.

search_vector_roadmap_steps.title: Credenciais e objetos S3 configurados
search_vector_roadmap_steps.desc: Usar credenciais configuradas para listar os objetos do bucket e selecionar PDFs novos ou alterados.

search_vector_roadmap_steps.title: Extracao e fragmentacao deterministica

search_columnar_subtitle: The columnar index answers analytical queries (count, sum, avg, min, max, with GROUP BY and WHERE) from its own entries when every column the query uses has a COLUMNAR index; EXPLAIN shows COLUMNAR_AGG. Other queries read the documents. Replaces dedicated column stores like ClickHouse for aggregation within AxonBase.
search_columnar_what_desc: The columnar index stores each column separately with sortable value encoding (null, bool, long, double, string, array, object). The key follows the format CI|{ns}|{db}|{table}|{index}|{column}|{typeByte}{encodedData}{rowKey}. This allows scanning column values without deserializing entire documents.
search_columnar_advantages_list: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX without loading documents: aggregation reads only the indexed column
Less memory and CPU: values stored in sortable binary format, no JSON
Efficient linear scan: CI| prefix is contiguous in RocksDB, no random seeks
ZSTD compression in RocksDB drastically reduces repetitive columnar data size
Automatic maintenance on CREATE, UPDATE, and DELETE with no intervention
EXPLAIN shows COLUMNAR strategy when planner detects equality or eligible aggregation

search_columnar_agg_desc: The planner automatically detects aggregation functions with arguments on indexed columns and uses the columnar index instead of loading documents. The result is computed by scanning only the column bytes.

search_columnar_eq_desc: The columnar index also accelerates WHERE column = value queries. The sortable encoder produces an exact key, enabling direct seek on the CI| prefix without scanning the table.

search_columnar_when_desc: Use columnar indexes on tables with many rows (100K+) when you frequently run aggregations like dashboards, reports, or count/sum/avg/min/max queries. The gain is larger when indexed columns have numeric types or short strings with high repetition. Does not replace UNIQUE indexes for exact equality lookup in OLTP tables — use the appropriate index type for each query pattern. Unlike SEARCH, GEO, and HNSW indexes, the columnar index does not use approximate search or ranking: it is deterministic and serves pure analytical aggregation.

dblink_intro: DATABASE LINK connects to remote AxonBase servers and makes their tables accessible as if they were local. Use the syntax "link_name"."table_name" in SELECT, JOIN, and subqueries. Tables without a prefix always resolve to the local database — existing queries work unchanged.
dblink_create_desc: Use CREATE DATABASE LINK to register a remote server. Provide the WebSocket URL, namespace, database, and optional credentials. The link is stored in the catalog and replicated via Raft like any other DDL.
dblink_query_desc: Prefix the table name with the link name and a dot: "link_name"."table_name". All SELECT operations work: WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, GROUP BY, functions, graph traversals, and full-text/vector/geo search are pushed down to the remote server.
dblink_join_desc: JOIN any combination of local tables, link tables, and local qualified tables. When both sides of a JOIN are on the same link, the join is executed remotely (pushdown). When sides are on different links, results are fetched in parallel and joined locally.
dblink_join_code:
-- Local + remote JOIN
SELECT u.name, o.total
FROM users u
JOIN "europe"."orders" o ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE u.age > 25;

-- JOIN between two remote databases
SELECT e.name, a.name
FROM "europe"."customers" e
JOIN "asia"."customers" a ON e.email = a.email;

-- Two tables from the same link (pushdown)
SELECT u.name, o.total
FROM "europe"."users" u
JOIN "europe"."orders" o ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE u.age > 25;
dblink_drop_desc: Use DROP DATABASE LINK to remove a registered link. Connections to the remote server are closed. Queries referencing the link name will fail until the link is recreated.
dblink_performance_desc: DATABASE LINK uses HTTP POST to the remote server's /sql endpoint. Connections are pooled and reused. The query is sent as-is with the remote namespace and database headers — the remote server executes it natively. Pushdown optimizations (WHERE, LIMIT, ORDER BY, JOIN, GROUP BY) are applied automatically: if all referenced columns belong to the same link, the entire filtered query is sent remotely, minimizing data transfer. For JOINs across different links, results are fetched in parallel and processed locally.
dblink_notes_desc: DATABASE LINK accepts SELECT, CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, and RELATE. The link name is defined with CREATE DATABASE LINK.
saga_intro: A SAGA coordinates changes across independent AxonBase databases. The orchestrator sends operations to participants and issues CANCEL SAGA when any step fails, triggering local compensation.
saga_architecture_desc: BEGIN SAGA, COMMIT SAGA, and CANCEL SAGA always go to the orchestrator. Each participant database runs its own local transaction.

import uvicorn
from fastapi import FastAPI, Header
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column

from axonbase.sqlalchemy import SagaExecuteTransaction
from sqlalchemy_common import engine

class Base(DeclarativeBase): pass

class Payment(Base):
    __tablename__ = "payment"
    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    status: Mapped[str]

app = FastAPI(title="payment-service")

ORCHESTRATOR = engine(8000, "orchestrator")

def create_order(order_id: str, x_correlation_id: str | None = Header(default=None)):
    correlation_id = x_correlation_id or f"order_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    with SagaExecuteTransaction(ORCHESTRATOR, PAYMENTS, "pedido") as transaction:

        request = Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:9102/invoices?order_id={order_id}", headers={"X-Correlation-Id": correlation_id}, method="POST")
        with urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
            response.read()
        transaction.commit()
    return {"status": "COMMITTED"}

saga_join_leave_desc: JOIN SAGA binds an active saga to the current session, ensuring all subsequent writes are recorded as saga steps. LEAVE SAGA unbinds the session without affecting the saga lifecycle. These commands are the secure alternative to setting $saga_corr directly.
saga_join_desc: Validates that the saga is RUNNING in the ledger, then binds (sagaName, correlationId) to the session. The validation and binding are atomic on the server, so a concurrent request cannot hijack the correlation.
saga_leave_desc: Clears the saga binding from the session. Idempotent: calling LEAVE SAGA on a session that is not in a saga is a no-op.
data_rules_intro: Data Rules are row-level and column-level security policies applied to the queries and writes of the authenticated user. The paths a rule does not cover are listed at the end of this page.
data_rules_how_desc: When a user executes a query, the system applies the data rule predicate as an additional condition on the rows read and written. An assigned rule that does not exist in the current database denies access, and so does a rule that needs a value the session does not have. A data rule is not a complete isolation boundary: see the limits below.
data_rules_create_desc: Use CREATE DATA RULE to define a predicate. The predicate can reference $token fields from the authenticated JWT.

CREATE USER alice ON ROOT

  APPLY DATA RULE region_sp, sales_usa;
data_rules_inject_desc: When the Data Rule predicate has the form field = value (field = $auth.field or field = literal), AxonBase automatically fills that field in INSERT and CREATE, overwriting any value sent by the user. In SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE, the field is used only as a filter and is never changed.
data_rules_mask_desc: The optional MASK FIELDS WITH clause hides the values of top level fields that match the patterns, for users who have the rule assigned. Hidden fields appear as *** in queries (including SELECT VALUE, aliases, access by id and FETCH) and in write responses.
data_rules_drop_desc: Use DROP DATA RULE to remove a rule. Users that still have the rule assigned are denied access until the rule is created again or the user is redefined without it.
data_rules_show_desc: Use SHOW DATA RULES para ver todas as regras definidas e seus predicados.
data_rules_auth_desc: $auth and $token hold the claims of the session token, and $auth.id is the user name. An authenticated session cannot set these variables. A user with a data rule cannot open LIVE SELECT or use /export.
data_rules_limits_title: What a data rule does not cover
data_rules_limits_items: WHERE and ORDER BY on a masked field use the real value, which can therefore be inferred.
A write that copies a masked field into another field of the same row (SET copy = cpf) exposes the value.
Masks do not reach nested fields such as address.cpf.
Edge properties read through graph traversal are not masked.
The AUDIT_LOG and AUDIT_CASES virtual tables show the original content.
The body of a DEFINE EVENT receives $before and $after without masks.
Functions that read storage directly, such as kv::, and queries sent through a DATABASE LINK.
Schema statements such as DROP TABLE, as well as RELATE and UNRELATE, are not restricted by the rule.
Error messages, such as a unique index violation, can reveal that a hidden value exists.
A program declared SECURITY DEFINER runs with the rules of its owner.
Backup and management routes, which require an administrative role.
data_rules_diagram_alt: Data Rules diagram: a user with an assigned rule sends a query, AxonBase injects the predicate and masks fields.
data_rules_demo_desc: The following commands create two orders, define a rule, assign it to a user, and demonstrate the effect.
data_rules_demo_setup:
# Creates table and inserts data
curl -s --data 'CREATE TABLE orders SCHEMALESS'
data_rules_demo_filter:
# Autentica como alice
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST -d '{"user":"alice","pass":"secret"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/signin | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get('token',''))")

# SELECT retorna apenas order 100 (sales_rep_id=165)
curl -s --data 'SELECT * FROM orders' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql
# Resultado: [{"sales_rep_id":165,"cpf":"***","credit_card":"***","product":"Laptop","id":"orders:100"}]
data_rules_demo_mask:
# UPDATE affects only order 100
curl -s --data 'UPDATE orders SET total'
data_rules_demo_inject:
# Create Data Rule with automatic injection.
curl -s --data "CREATE DATA RULE publisher_only APPLY publisher_id = 42" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer root' http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql

# Create user with the rule.
curl -s --data "CREATE USER bob ON ROOT PASSWORD 'bob' ROLES editor APPLY DATA RULE publisher_only" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer root' http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql

# Bob creates an article without publisher_id - 42 is injected.
TOKEN_BOB=$(curl -s -X POST -d '{"user":"bob","pass":"bob"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/signin | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d.get('token',''))")
curl -s --data 'CREATE article CONTENT { title: "Bob's post" }' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_BOB" http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql

# Bob tries to bypass with another publisher_id - it is overwritten to 42.
curl -s --data 'CREATE article CONTENT { title: "Attempt", publisher_id: 99 }' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_BOB" http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql

# Verify: all of Bob's articles have publisher_id = 42.
curl -s --data 'SELECT * FROM article' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_BOB" http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql
# Result: all with publisher_id=42
data_rules_demo_drop:
# Remove a regra
curl -s --data 'DROP DATA RULE region_sp' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer root' http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql
config_docker_title: Docker: pass configuration via environment variables
config_docker_desc: Every option has an AXON_* environment variable. Pass them with -e on docker run or in the environment section of docker-compose.yml. This is the recommended way to configure containers, since it keeps secrets out of the image and lets each node differ.
config_docker_code:
docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8000:8000 \
  -e AXON_REQUIRE_AUTH=false \
  -e AXON_S3_ENDPOINT=http://minio:9000 \
  -e AXON_S3_BUCKET=my-backups \
  -e AXON_S3_ACCESS=minioadmin \
  -e AXON_S3_SECRET=minioadmin \
  -e AXON_S3_INTERVAL=60000 \
  -e AXON_S3_RETENTION=10 \
  axonbase/axonbase:latest
config_file_desc: Alternatively, mount a full axonbase.conf file into the container. The server reads it on startup before applying environment variables. Use this when you have a long, static configuration or want to version it.
config_file_code:
# Local file axonbase.conf
path = data
bind = 0.0.0.0
port = 8000
require_auth = false
s3_endpoint = http://minio:9000
s3_bucket = my-backups
s3_access = minioadmin
s3_secret = minioadmin
s3_interval = 60000

# Mount it into the container
docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8000:8000 \
  -v $PWD/axonbase.conf:/app/axonbase.conf \
  -v axonbase-data:/data \
  axonbase/axonbase:latest
config_example_desc: This example starts AxonBase with RocksDB storage on a named volume, enables authentication, and sets the root user and password. Data persists across restarts on the axonbase-data volume.
config_example_code:
docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8000:8000 \
  -v axonbase-data:/data \
  -e AXON_PATH=/data \
  -e AXON_BIND=0.0.0.0 \
  -e AXON_REQUIRE_AUTH=true \
  -e AXON_SECRET=change-me-signing-secret \
  -e AXON_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me-root-password \
  axonbase/axonbase:latest
config_example_signin_desc: With authentication enabled, sign in over HTTP to obtain a JWT, then use it in subsequent requests.
config_cert_desc: Configure TLS with a PKCS12 keystore and a JKS truststore for mutual TLS (mTLS). The CA in the truststore must issue the client certificates that will authenticate.
config_cert_code:
docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8443:8000 \
  -v axonbase-data:/data \
  -v $PWD/certs:/etc/axonbase/certs:ro \
  -e AXON_PATH=/data \
  -e AXON_BIND=0.0.0.0 \
  -e AXON_REQUIRE_AUTH=true \
  -e AXON_TLS_CERT=/etc/axonbase/certs/server/server.p12 \
  -e AXON_TLS_KEY=changeit \
  -e AXON_TLS_CA=/etc/axonbase/certs/truststores/icpbrasil.jks \
  axonbase/axonbase:latest
config_cert_login_desc: Present the client certificate in the TLS handshake. The endpoint validates the chain against the truststore, extracts CPF or CNPJ when configured with ICPBRASIL, and returns an axontc_ temporary credential. Use that credential as the password in signin to obtain a JWT.
config_cert_login_code:
curl -k https://127.0.0.1:8443/certificate/login/icp_brasil?ns=test\&db=dev \
  --cert client.pem --key client.key
# Returns an axontc_ temporary credential, e.g.:
# {"credential":"axontc_...", "user":"12345678901", "expiresIn":60}

# Use the credential as password in signin:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/signin \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"user":"12345678901","pass":"axontc_..."}'
config_cert_rpc_desc: For applications that cannot present a certificate in a TLS handshake, use the certificate.begin and certificate.complete RPC flow. begin returns a 32-byte Base64URL challenge; sign the exact ASCII bytes with the client private key and send the DER Base64 certificate chain to complete.
config_cert_rpc_code:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"id":1,"method":"certificate.begin","params":[{"store":"icp_brasil"}]}'
# -> {"id":"...","challenge":"<base64url>","expiresAt":"..."}

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"id":2,"method":"certificate.complete","params":[{"id":"...","challenge":"<same base64url>","store":"icp_brasil","user":"12345678901","chain":["<DER base64>"],"signature":"<base64>"}]}'
# -> { "credential": "axontc_...", "user": "12345678901" }
config_precedence_desc: Values are applied in this order, each overriding the previous: default (1) < axonbase.conf file (2) < AXON_* environment variables (3) < CLI flags (4).
config_example_flow_title: Complete Flow: Start, Sign In, and Query
config_example_flow_desc: Start AxonBase with authentication enabled, sign in to obtain a JWT token, and use it in subsequent SQL queries. The token is sent via the Authorization: Bearer header.
config_example_flow_code:
# 1. Start server with auth enabled
docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8000:8000 \
  -v axonbase-data:/data \
  -e AXON_PATH=/data \
  -e AXON_BIND=0.0.0.0 \
  -e AXON_REQUIRE_AUTH=true \
  -e AXON_SECRET=change-me-signing-secret \
  -e AXON_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me-root-password \
  axonbase/axonbase:latest

# 2. Sign in and capture the JWT token
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/signin \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"user":"root","pass":"change-me-root-password"}' \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['token'])")

echo "Token: $TOKEN"

# 3. Create data using the token
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer '$TOKEN \
  -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' \
  --data 'CREATE person CONTENT {name: "Ana", age: 30}'

# 4. Query data
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer '$TOKEN \
  -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' \
  --data 'SELECT * FROM person'
ai_audit_intro: AI Audit turns a natural-language policy into local audit rules. The AI is called only while creating the audit. Every later command is classified inside AxonBase, without sending production SQL to the provider.
ai_audit_diagram_alt: AI Audit workflow illustration: a policy moves through rule generation, an inspection gateway, and three paths for safe execution, review, and blocking.
ai_audit_diagram_caption: Image generated with fal.ai. Labels and decisions remain in the local AxonBase engine.
ai_audit_flow_intro: Creation materializes the rules. Later execution uses only those rules and records decisions that need human intervention.

ai_audit_flow.label: Define the policy
ai_audit_flow.text: Describe what deserves review and what must be blocked.

ai_audit_flow.label: Generate rules
ai_audit_flow.text: CREATE AI AUDIT calls the provider once and saves the resulting rules in the catalog.

ai_audit_flow.label: Classify locally
ai_audit_flow.text: SAFE continues immediately. WARNING opens a pending case. DANGER blocks the user.

ai_audit_flow.label: Resolve the case
ai_audit_flow.text: An operator records the reason and authorizes or denies the original operation.

ai_audit_create_desc: The two prompts separate operations that need approval from prohibited operations. Prefer objective criteria and mention the AxonQL syntax used by the team.
ai_audit_config_desc: Configure the provider and model on the server. ai_base_url supports Ollama or an organization-hosted compatible endpoint.
ai_audit_config_env:
AXON_AI_PROVIDER=openai
AXON_AI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini
AXON_AI_API_KEY=$OPENAI_API_KEY

# Ollama or a compatible endpoint
AXON_AI_PROVIDER=ollama
AXON_AI_MODEL=qwen3-coder:latest
AXON_AI_API_KEY=ollama
AXON_AI_BASE_URL=http://ollama.internal:11434
ai_audit_config_file:
ai_provider = openai
ai_model = gpt-4o-mini
ai_api_key = ${OPENAI_API_KEY}

# Ollama or a compatible endpoint
ai_provider = ollama
ai_model = qwen3-coder:latest
ai_api_key = ollama
ai_base_url = http://ollama.internal:11434
ai_audit_assign_desc: The AUDITED BY clause attaches the user to an audit. Only that user's commands pass through the materialized rules.
ai_audit_assign_code:
CREATE USER alice ON DATABASE
  PASSWORD 'secret'
  ROLES editor
  AUDITED BY protect_production;
ai_audit_safe_desc: The command does not match a rule and runs normally.
ai_audit_warning_desc: The command remains pending until someone records an explicit decision.
ai_audit_danger_desc: The operation is rejected and the user stays blocked until authorization.
ai_audit_resolve_desc: Authorization executes the original SQL exactly once with an audit bypass, avoiding a second case for the same operation.
ai_audit_resolve_code:
SET REASON AUDIT CASE 'a8d4...' 'Cleanup approved for the maintenance window';
SET AUDIT CASE 'a8d4...' AUTHORIZED REASON 'Change registered in ticket OPS-218';
ai_audit_cases_desc: AUDIT_CASES is a virtual table with the original SQL, classification, user, reason, resolution, and case events.
ai_audit_diagram_footer: AI creates the rules. AxonBase makes every runtime decision.

use_cases_intro: From financial services to healthcare, AxonBase replaces multiple specialized systems with a single engine, reducing infrastructure complexity, operational cost, and security risk.
use_cases_positioning_text: AxonBase is the database for microservices and AI agents that need distributed transactions, AI governance, and multi-model search, all in a single SQL engine.

use_cases_positioning.title: What Makes AxonBase Different
use_cases_positioning.subtitle: Three capabilities that no other database combines in a single engine:
features: Distributed transactions via native sagas: BEGIN SAGA, COMMIT SAGA, CANCEL SAGA with correlation, compensation, and remote rollback
AI governance with AI Audit: LLM-generated rules classify every query as SAFE, WARNING, or DANGER before execution, without sending production data to the AI provider
Multi-model search in one engine: BM25 full-text, HNSW vectors, GeoJSON spatial, graph traversal, and columnar aggregation, all in a single AxonQL statement

use_cases_sectors_intro: Each sector benefits from a different combination of AxonBase capabilities. The engine adapts to the data shape, not the other way around.

use_cases_sectors.title: Banking and Financial Services
use_cases_sectors.pain: Banks need ACID transactions, audit trails, and role-based access across millions of accounts, with real-time fraud detection and strict regulatory compliance.
capabilities: Sagas for distributed ledger transactions across core banking systems, with automatic compensation on failure
Data Rules with field masking to protect PII (CPF, account numbers, credit cards) without modifying application code
AI Audit to classify every query as SAFE, WARNING, or DANGER before execution, meeting Bacen and LGPD requirements
mTLS and certificate-based authentication (ICP-Brasil compatible) for secure inter-bank communication
Columnar indexes for real-time aggregation of balances, transaction counts, and risk metrics without ETL

use_cases_sectors.title: Fintech and Payments
use_cases_sectors.pain: Fintechs move fast but cannot compromise on compliance. They need a database that supports rapid iteration, auditability, and multi-tenant isolation from day one.
capabilities: Multi-tenant by design: namespaces and databases isolate each client or product line with zero configuration
Graph relations for payment flows, wallet hierarchies, and recommendation networks in a single query
Live queries for real-time balance updates, transaction notifications, and fraud alerts over WebSocket
JDBC driver for existing BI tools, plus GraphQL and REST for mobile and web backends
Scalable from startup MVP to millions of users with the same RocksDB-backed engine

use_cases_sectors.title: Government and Public Sector
use_cases_sectors.pain: Governments require data sovereignty, auditability, and ICP-Brasil certificate support. They cannot afford vendor lock-in or cloud-only solutions.
capabilities: Certificate-based authentication with ICP-Brasil trust store for digital signatures and identity verification
AI Audit for automated compliance verification of every data access and modification
Data Rules with field masking to protect citizen PII across all queries without application changes
Self-hosted deployment with no cloud dependency: RocksDB persistence, S3 backup, and Raft cluster
Full audit trail via S3 backup encryption (AES-256-GCM) and export/import for data portability

use_cases_sectors.title: Healthtech and Healthcare
use_cases_sectors.pain: Healthcare applications handle sensitive patient data, require strict access control, and need to query structured records, clinical notes, and medical images in a compliant way.
capabilities: Data Rules with field masking to protect patient PII (name, CPF, diagnosis) without touching application code
AI Audit to classify every query and block unauthorized access to patient records
BM25 full-text search over clinical notes, prescriptions, and medical reports with relevance ranking
HNSW vector search for semantic similarity over medical embeddings and imaging metadata
Sagas for distributed healthcare workflows: appointment scheduling, lab results, and billing across systems

use_cases_sectors.title: E-Commerce and Marketplace
use_cases_sectors.pain: E-commerce platforms need real-time product search, personalized recommendations, inventory management, and order processing, all with high availability.
capabilities: BM25 full-text search for product catalogs with relevance ranking and highlighting
HNSW vector search for semantic product recommendations and visual similarity
Graph traversal for recommendation networks: customers who bought X also bought Y
Geo search for local inventory, store locators, and delivery radius queries
Live queries for real-time inventory updates, order status changes, and price alerts via WebSocket

use_cases_sectors.title: IoT and Telemetry
use_cases_sectors.pain: IoT systems ingest millions of data points per second, need time-series aggregation, geospatial queries, and real-time alerting with minimal operational overhead.
capabilities: Columnar indexes for real-time aggregation of count, sum, avg, min, max over sensor data without loading raw documents
Geo search for location-based queries: devices within a radius, fleet tracking, geofence alerts
Live queries for real-time telemetry streaming and threshold alerts over WebSocket
Raft cluster for high availability and automatic failover in distributed sensor networks
RocksDB storage for high-ingestion throughput (243K inserts/s in batch)

use_cases_sectors.title: Legal and Compliance
use_cases_sectors.pain: Legal departments manage contracts, litigation documents, and regulatory filings that require full-text search, version history, and strict access control.
capabilities: BM25 full-text search over legal documents with configurable analyzers, stopwords, and stemming
Data Rules to enforce attorney-client privilege and document-level access control
AI Audit to classify queries and prevent unauthorized access to sensitive legal content
Sagas for distributed contract lifecycle management: drafting, review, approval, and signing
Export/import for data portability and archival compliance

use_cases_comparison_intro: Organizations today stitch together multiple systems to solve one problem. AxonBase replaces them with a single engine.

adminapi_intro: The management API (Application Programming Interface) answers under /admin/v1 on the same port as the data endpoints. Every response is JSON (JavaScript Object Notation). It covers server information, users, service tokens, cluster, sagas, audit, security and backups. It reuses the engine, so roles and scope are the ones the engine enforces.
adminapi_auth_desc: Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. The token is a JWT (JSON Web Token) from POST /signin, or a service token (axsvc_...) created through the API. With require_auth set to false, every call runs as an anonymous admin and the header is optional.
adminapi_auth_code:
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/signin \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"user":"root","pass":"change-me-root-password"}' \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['token'])")

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/info -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
adminapi_roles_desc: There are three roles, in increasing order of power: viewer, operator and admin. The owner role counts as admin. A ROOT identity with no recognized role is treated as admin; an identity of another scope with no recognized role has no role and receives 403 on role-checked routes. Most routes require ROOT scope. Routes that take ns and db (tables, data-rules, audit/operations and audit/definitions) also accept an identity whose scope covers that database, with at least the viewer role. A role that is explicitly viewer is read-only in the engine (writes, DDL, kv::set and kv::del are refused); an identity with no recognized role is not made read-only. See Security, including the Axon-Role-Cap header that lowers the role of one request.
adminapi_roles_rows: All read routes: info, namespaces, tables, users, cluster, sagas, audit, data rules, truststores, certificates and events.
Everything viewer does, plus cancel sagas, decide audit cases, unblock users, and list, check and trigger backups.
Everything operator does, plus create and delete users, manage service tokens and truststores, and restore backups.
adminapi_errors_desc: An error returns the HTTP status and a JSON body with code and message. NOT_LEADER also carries leader and leaderAddress. Messages follow the server language (AXON_LANG).
adminapi_errors_rows: Token missing, invalid, expired or revoked.
The role or the scope is not enough.
Unknown route or method, or the resource does not exist.
Invalid JSON, field or parameter, or an engine error such as a rejected statement.
State conflict: audit case already decided, saga that cannot be cancelled, backup already running or not configured, restore not allowed.
A write reached a follower. Repeat it on leaderAddress.
Unexpected failure. The detail goes to the server log.
adminapi_conv_desc: Writes that change replicated state (create and delete users, cancel a saga, decide an audit case, unblock a user) run only on the leader. Service tokens, truststores and backups act on the node that receives the call. Timestamps follow RFC (Request for Comments) 3339 in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). List routes that accept limit return 100 items by default and at most 1000. DELETE and unblock answer 204 with no body.
adminapi_endpoints_desc: The role column is the minimum required. Scoped means a ROOT identity, or an identity whose scope covers the database.
adminapi_endpoints_rows: Version, node, role, uptime, mode and the non-secret configuration.
Tables with schema mode, fields and indexes.
Row count, fields, indexes, geoFields and vectorFields of one table.
Users with scope, roles and authentication kind. Never returns hashes.
Creates a user (runs DEFINE USER with the caller's claims). Leader only.
Deletes the user of that exact scope. ns and db go in the query string. Leader only.
Lists service tokens without the secret.
Creates a service token. The secret appears only in this response.
Revokes the token. It stops working immediately.
Mode, leader, term, commit index, quorum and members with lag.
Cancels a running saga (CANCEL SAGA). Leader only.
AI audit cases from every database. Filters: status, limit.
Authorizes or denies a pending case (SET AUDIT CASE). Leader only.
Unblocks the user in every database. Leader only.
Operation audit entries, newest first. Requires ns and db. Filters: from, limit.
AI audit definitions of a database. Requires ns and db.
Data rules of a database: predicate, mask patterns and injections. Requires ns and db.
Uploads and registers a JKS (Java KeyStore) as multipart/form-data.
Removes the truststore from the registry.
Certificates that expire within days (default 30), including expired ones.
Backups in remote storage with size, date and type.
State of the backup scheduler and of the last run.
Starts a backup in the background (202). Body: type auto or full.
Restores up to the named backup. Requires confirm.
Streams the whole instance as an .axbak file. Query: type (full or incremental), since. See Backup.
Restores the instance from an .axbak body. Query: confirm, force. 409 in a cluster. See Backup.
SSE (Server-Sent Events) stream. See Events and Webhook.
Last lines of the in-memory log buffer. Filters: limit, level, since.
SSE stream of new log lines, one data: line per entry.
adminapi_ex_info_desc: The response never includes the JWT secret, the root password or the S3 keys. The config object is shortened here.
adminapi_ex_catalog_desc: index.kind is one of standard, unique, search, vector, geo or columnar. schemaMode is SCHEMAFULL or SCHEMALESS.
adminapi_ex_users_desc: name must be an identifier (letters, digits and underscore, starting with a letter). scope is ROOT, NAMESPACE or DATABASE; ns and db are required according to the scope. roles is optional. The call runs DEFINE USER with the caller's claims, so a caller cannot create an identity broader than its own. Deleting needs the scope in the path and ns and db in the query string.
adminapi_ex_users_code:
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"name":"ana","scope":"DATABASE","ns":"app","db":"main","password":"s3cret","roles":["viewer"]}'
# 201 {"name":"ana","scope":"DATABASE","ns":"app","db":"main","roles":["viewer"]}

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/users -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# [{"name":"ana","scope":"DATABASE","ns":"app","db":"main","roles":["viewer"],"auth":"password"}]

curl -s -X DELETE "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/users/DATABASE/ana?ns=app&db=main" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 204
adminapi_ex_tokens_desc: name is required. scope defaults to ROOT, roles to ["viewer"] and expiresInDays to 90 (allowed range 1 to 3650). The token field is returned once. Rules and limits are in Security.
adminapi_ex_tokens_code:
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/service-tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"name":"grafana","roles":["viewer"],"expiresInDays":30}'
# 201 {"id":"9f2c1a0b7d3e","token":"axsvc_9f2c1a0b7d3e_...","expiresAt":"2026-12-23T12:00:00Z"}

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/service-tokens -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

events_webhook_desc: Set AXON_WEBHOOK_URL and the server sends each event to that URL with POST and Content-Type application/json, with a 5 second timeout. There is no retry: a failure or a status of 300 or higher is logged as webhook_failed and the event is not sent again. With AXON_WEBHOOK_SECRET set, the request carries three headers: X-Axon-Timestamp (Unix seconds at sending time), X-Axon-Signature-V2: sha256=<hex> and the older X-Axon-Signature: sha256=<hex>. In both signatures <hex> is the HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) with SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256) keyed with the secret. The old one covers only the exact request body. The V2 one covers the text timestamp.body (the timestamp, a dot and the exact body), so a receiver can reject a delivery that someone captured and replays later. The old header stays for compatibility with existing receivers; new ones should verify V2. Without a secret no signature header is sent, and the server logs a warn entry named webhook_unsigned.
events_verify_desc: Compute the HMAC over the raw bytes, before any JSON parsing, and compare in constant time. For V2 the signed text is the value of X-Axon-Timestamp, a dot and the exact body. Also check the timestamp against the clock of the receiver with a tolerance window (the examples use 5 minutes): a valid signature on an old timestamp is a replay. Re-serializing the JSON changes the bytes and breaks the check. To keep verifying the old header instead, compute the HMAC of the body alone and compare it with X-Axon-Signature.
events_verify_python:
import hashlib
import hmac
import os
import time

from flask import Flask, abort, request

app = Flask(__name__)
SECRET = os.environ["AXON_WEBHOOK_SECRET"].encode()
TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300  # 5 minutes: rejects replayed deliveries


@app.post("/axonbase-hook")
def hook():
    body = request.get_data()  # bytes exactly as received
    timestamp = request.headers.get("X-Axon-Timestamp", "")
    received = request.headers.get("X-Axon-Signature-V2", "")

    # reject old or future timestamps (replay protection)
    try:
        age = abs(time.time() - float(timestamp))
    except ValueError:
        abort(401)
    if age > TOLERANCE_SECONDS:
        abort(401)

    # the signature covers "timestamp.body"
    signed = timestamp.encode() + b"." + body
    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(SECRET, signed, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(received, expected):
        abort(401)

    event = request.get_json()
    print(event["type"], event["data"])
    return "", 204


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(port=9000)
security_rbac_desc: The engine checks the role of every session that carries an identity. A session without identity (embedded mode, or a server with require_auth set to false) is not restricted. The roles are viewer, operator and admin, in increasing order; owner counts as admin. A ROOT identity with no recognized role counts as admin, so older ROOT users keep working. An identity of another scope with no recognized role (for example, only a custom role such as editor) can still read and write data allowed by table PERMISSIONS, but it cannot run the statements below. Reads and writes of data are governed by PERMISSIONS, not by these roles.
security_rbac_rows: DEFINE USER, CREATE USER, DROP USER
DEFINE ACCESS, GRANT ACCESS, REVOKE ACCESS
CREATE DATA RULE, DROP DATA RULE
AI audit definitions (CREATE AI AUDIT and its removal)
operator (only an explicit viewer is refused, see below)
security_rbac_scope: Scope has its own rule: a user below ROOT never creates an identity with a broader scope than its own, nor one outside its own namespace or database. The attempt fails with: creating an identity with a broader scope than your own is not allowed. A user blocked by AI audit cannot decide the audit case that blocked them.
security_rbac_code:
-- Session of a DATABASE user whose roles are "editor" (no recognized role):
CREATE person:1 CONTENT {name: "Ana"};          -- allowed by table PERMISSIONS
DEFINE USER bob ON DATABASE PASSWORD "x";       -- error: operation requires the admin role

-- Session of a DATABASE admin of app/main:
DEFINE USER bob ON DATABASE PASSWORD "x";       -- allowed
DEFINE USER eve ON NAMESPACE PASSWORD "x";      -- error: broader scope than your own
security_readonly_desc: A session whose role is explicitly viewer is read-only, and the engine enforces it: every write and DDL (Data Definition Language) statement is refused, and so are kv::set and kv::del. The rule holds on every data route: /sql (SQL, Structured Query Language), /rpc (RPC, Remote Procedure Call), /table, /graphql, /mcp (MCP, Model Context Protocol) and /import. Over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) a write on /sql answers 400, /import answers 403, and over RPC the error code is -32002 with the message read-only session: write refused. Reads keep working. The exception is an identity with no recognized role (role NONE): such legacy tokens, for example the ones the SDKs obtain for a DATABASE scope, behave as before and are not made read-only.

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_TOKEN" -H "Axon-Ns: loja" -H "Axon-Db: ops" \
  -d 'SELECT * FROM itens'
# 200

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_TOKEN" -H "Axon-Ns: loja" -H "Axon-Db: ops" \
  -d 'DELETE itens:1'
# 400 (read-only session: write refused); the same refusal for CREATE, UPDATE and kv::set

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/import \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_TOKEN" -H "Axon-Ns: loja" -H "Axon-Db: ops" \
  -d 'DELETE itens:1;'
# 403
security_cap_desc: The Axon-Role-Cap header lets the caller lower the role of a single request. Accepted values are viewer and operator. It only lowers, never raises: a token that is already at or below the cap passes unchanged, and one with no recognized role is not affected. With viewer the request is read-only. With operator the request works as an admin without the statements that need the admin role: users (DEFINE USER and the like), access, JKS (Java KeyStore) truststores, data rules, AI audit definitions, database links and sagas. Any other value answers 400 on every route. The use case is an intermediate service that holds a powerful token but wants to limit what each call can do, for example a backend that serves reports and sends viewer on every request.

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROOT_TOKEN" -H "Axon-Ns: loja" -H "Axon-Db: ops" \
  -H "Axon-Role-Cap: viewer" -d 'DELETE itens:1'

# operator cap: data writes work, user definitions do not

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROOT_TOKEN" -H "Axon-Ns: loja" -H "Axon-Db: ops" \
  -H "Axon-Role-Cap: operator" -d 'DEFINE USER x ON DATABASE PASSWORD "p"'
# 400

# unknown value
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROOT_TOKEN" -H "Axon-Role-Cap: admin" -d 'SELECT 1'
# 400
security_use_desc: USE ns db now respects the scope of the token. Before, a DATABASE or NAMESPACE token could switch to another namespace or database with USE inside a SQL batch and read data outside its scope. Now the target is checked before the switch and a destination outside the scope is refused with the error code -32002. A ROOT token can still switch anywhere.
security_root_desc: At startup the server registers the root user. The name and the password come from AXON_ROOT_USER and AXON_ROOT_PASSWORD (keys root_user and root_password in axonbase.conf). A blank password (empty or only spaces) is refused at startup, in every environment, not only on a non-loopback bind.
security_insecure_desc: With authentication on (require_auth true) and a bind address that is not loopback, the server refuses to start while the root password is still root or the JWT secret is still the default. It prints the reason on stderr and exits with code 2. Loopback means an empty bind, localhost, ::1 or an address starting with 127. Set AXON_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEFAULTS=true to start anyway, for a throwaway environment. The variable is read only from the environment.

security_svc_desc: A service token is a long-lived credential for agents and integrations, such as a metrics scraper or an alert bridge. Its format is axsvc_<id>_<secret>. Create it with POST /admin/v1/service-tokens (admin role) and send it as Authorization: Bearer, exactly like a JWT. The secret is shown once, in the creation response; the server keeps only its SHA-256 hash. Each token has a name, a scope (ROOT, NAMESPACE or DATABASE), roles (viewer, operator or admin; default viewer) and an expiry between 1 and 3650 days (default 90). Revoking with DELETE /admin/v1/service-tokens/{id} takes effect immediately. The list shows lastUsedAt, which is saved at most once per minute.

backup_state_desc: With S3 configured, GET /admin/v1/backups/status returns configured, running, lastSuccessAt, lastErrorAt, lastError, lastDurationMs, lastSizeBytes, lastType and nextRunAt. Fields with no value yet are null; without S3, configured is false. GET /admin/v1/backups lists the backups in the bucket, oldest first, with name, sizeBytes, createdAt and type (full or incremental). sizeBytes and type are null for files that have no recorded metadata. createdAt comes from the timestamp in the file name (cluster-yyyyMMdd-HHmmss.axbak), read in the server time zone. Both routes need the operator role.
backup_trigger_desc: POST /admin/v1/backups starts a run in the background and answers 202 with a runId. The body is optional: type is auto (default) or full. It answers 409 when S3 is not configured or when a backup is already running. To follow the result, poll the status route or listen for the backup.finished and backup.failed events.
backup_incremental_desc: With type auto, a run is incremental when the storage backend keeps key versions (RocksDB, WAL and memory do) and an earlier run of this process left a watermark. An incremental file carries only the keys written after that watermark, plus the control state. The watermark is the backend version counter, not the Raft commit index, which is a different unit. RocksDB starts its counter from the RocksDB sequence number when it opens, so versions keep growing across restarts. The watermark itself is kept in memory: the first backup after a restart is full. type full always forces a full backup.
backup_incremental_limits: Limitations: a deletion is carried as a tombstone only when the storage backend reports deletions after the watermark; in that case the incremental file has !del lines and a restore that replays the files in order removes the key. The tombstones are kept by the backend, not by the file: a backup is only complete when the whole chain (the full backup and every incremental after it) is restored. Retention (s3_retention) works on whole chains, as described below.
backup_api_restore_desc: POST /admin/v1/backups/{name}/restore needs the admin role and a body with confirm set to true. The server downloads every backup from the oldest up to the named one, decrypts them with s3_encrypt_key, merges them and loads the result. This restores the whole instance (every namespace), unlike POST /import, which loads a dump of one database. The checks run in this order: confirm missing gives 400; S3 not configured gives 409; unknown name gives 404; a node in a cluster gives 409, because restoring through this API is not supported in a cluster; storage that already has data gives 409 unless force is true. A failure while loading gives 500. After a successful restore the root user is registered again with the configured credentials.
backup_observe_desc: Each run updates the axe_backup_* series (see Observability) and publishes backup.finished or backup.failed (see Events and Webhook).
perf_intro: Query planning and the HTTP server avoid reading more than the statement needs, and refuse work instead of queueing it when the server is saturated. This page lists the conditions under which each optimization applies.
perf_select_desc: SELECT tries each index source in turn and falls back to scanning the table only when none applies. The scan is not computed beforehand, so an indexed query no longer reads the whole table first. The WHERE clause is still evaluated on every document the index returns.
perf_select_rows: FROM is a plain table and the whole WHERE is field = literal, with a single-column UNIQUE index on that field.
ORDER BY starts with vector::distance::... over a field with a vector index and a query vector of the right dimension.
The whole WHERE is geo::distance(field, point) < radius (or <=), with a geo index on the field.
The whole WHERE is field = literal, with a columnar index that includes the field. With no match, the query falls through to the next source.
WHERE uses MATCH over a field with a search index.
perf_limit_title: SELECT ... LIMIT reads in a stream
perf_limit_desc: When no index source applies, a SELECT with LIMIT reads the table in key order through an iterator and stops as soon as START + LIMIT documents pass WHERE, Data Rules and permissions. The query then costs about the size of the window, not the size of the table. RocksDB serves the iterator without holding the backend lock, so a long scan does not block writers. It applies only when all of these hold: FROM is a plain table, there is a LIMIT, and the statement has no ORDER BY, no JOIN, no GROUP BY, no aggregate function and no MATCH. Otherwise the whole table is read.
perf_limit_code:
SELECT * FROM event LIMIT 10;                      -- streams, stops after 10 rows
SELECT * FROM event WHERE level = "error" LIMIT 10; -- streams, stops after 10 matches
SELECT * FROM event ORDER BY ts LIMIT 10;          -- ORDER BY: reads the whole table
SELECT count() FROM event LIMIT 10;                -- aggregate: reads the whole table
perf_mutation_title: UPDATE and DELETE with an index
perf_mutation_desc: On a whole table, UPDATE and DELETE with WHERE field = literal pick their targets through the UNIQUE and columnar indexes, with the same conditions as SELECT, instead of listing every key. The WHERE is still re-evaluated on each document before it changes. Without a usable index, the table is listed as before.
perf_mutation_code:
UPDATE person SET active = false WHERE email = "ana@example.com";  -- via UNIQUE index
DELETE person WHERE email = "ana@example.com";                      -- via UNIQUE index
perf_admission_desc: A slow query must not take every HTTP worker thread and leave health probes and operations unanswered. The server therefore limits how many data requests run at once to http_threads minus a reserve of max(2, http_threads / 8). The default http_threads is 32, which reserves 4 threads and admits 28 data requests. A request beyond the limit is refused at once, without waiting in a queue, with 503 and Retry-After: 1. These paths are exempt, never counted and never refused: /health, /ready, /status, /version, /metrics, /admin (including /admin/v1) and the WebSocket upgrade at /rpc/ws. Every other path counts, including /sql, /rpc, /graphql and /signin. Clients should retry after the interval, with backoff.
