Retry-After: 1
Content-Type: application/json

{"status":"ERR","kind":"OVERLOADED","detail":"server busy"}

# Raise the pool (and with it the admitted requests)
AXON_HTTP_THREADS=64 ./run.sh start --port 8000   # reserve 8, admits 56
sql_ddl_unique_desc: CREATE INDEX ... UNIQUE on a table that already has records fills the index with the current values. If any value repeats, the statement is refused with a unique index violation and the index is not created; the check runs before anything is written, so a refusal leaves no partial entries. Records without the field stay out of the index, as in a normal write. Defining the same unique index again (same columns) does nothing. Changing the columns of an existing unique index checks the data again. Uniqueness compares the whole index entry, so values such as sfoo and foo, or 1 and n1, no longer collide.
config_secure_desc: On any bind address other than loopback, set the root password and the JWT secret before the first start. The server exits with code 2 otherwise. See Security for the rule and for AXON_ALLOW_INSECURE_DEFAULTS.
config_secure_code:
docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8000:8000 \
  -v axonbase-data:/data \
  -e AXON_PATH=/data \
  -e AXON_BIND=0.0.0.0 \
  -e AXON_SECRET=change-me-signing-secret \
  -e AXON_ROOT_USER=admin \
  -e AXON_ROOT_PASSWORD=change-me-root-password \
  axonbase/axonbase:latest
adminapi_ex_logs_desc: The server keeps the most recent log lines in memory (AXON_LOG_BUFFER lines, default 10000; the oldest is dropped when full, and everything is lost on restart). GET /admin/v1/logs returns them in chronological order. limit defaults to 500 and is capped by the buffer size; level is the minimum severity (debug, info, warn or error; an unknown value counts as info); since is an RFC 3339 instant. Each entry has ts, level, event, msg and fields. /admin/v1/logs/stream is an SSE stream with the same entries, only for lines written after the connection opens. Only lines produced by the structured logger enter the buffer.
adminapi_ex_logs_code:
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/logs?level=warn&limit=50&since=2026-11-23T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# [{"ts":"2026-11-23T14:05:09.311Z","level":"error","event":"backup_failed","msg":"backup.failed",
#   "fields":{"error":"connection refused","durationMs":812}}]

curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/logs/stream -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# : connected
#
# data: {"ts":"...","level":"info","event":"http_request","msg":"GET /health","fields":{...}}
backup_stream_desc: GET /admin/v1/backups/export streams the whole instance (every namespace, plus the control state) as an .axbak file, read from the storage and written straight to the HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) response. It needs the operator role and does not depend on S3. POST /admin/v1/backups/restore reads an .axbak file from the request body, line by line, and needs the admin role. Unlike GET /export and POST /import, which handle one database as an AxonQL dump, these two routes handle the whole instance. The export response is named axonbase-full-<version>.axbak or axonbase-incremental-<version>.axbak in Content-Disposition.
backup_stream_params_rows: full (default) or incremental. Any other value gives 400.
Required with type=incremental: a positive backend version, normally the X-Axon-Backup-Version of the previous export. Missing, zero or not a number gives 400.
true overwrites a storage that already has data; without it the answer is 409.
full or incremental, what was really written. If the storage backend does not keep key versions, an incremental request produces a full file and the header says full.
The backend version read before the dump started. Pass it as since in the next incremental export.
backup_stream_code:
# Full export (operator role). -D saves the response headers.
curl -s -D headers.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/backups/export?type=full" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o full.axbak
grep -i '^x-axon-backup' headers.txt
# X-Axon-Backup-Type: full
# X-Axon-Backup-Version: 48213        (example value)

# Incremental export: only what changed after that version, plus deletions
curl -s -D headers2.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/backups/export?type=incremental&since=48213" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o inc.axbak

# Restore on an empty node (admin role)
curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/backups/restore?confirm=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --data-binary @full.axbak
# {"restored":true,"restoredKeys":2048}        (example value)

# Overwrite a node that already has data
curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/backups/restore?confirm=true&force=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --data-binary @full.axbak
backup_stream_format_desc: The file is text. The first line is --axonbase-backup-v1--, followed by a ctrl line with the control state and one line per key (key, a tab, and the value in Base64). An incremental file carries only the keys written after since and, for each key deleted after since, a line !del with the key in Base64 (a tombstone). The restore applies the lines in order, so a tombstone removes the key. The incremental files that the S3 scheduler writes carry the same tombstones. With s3_encrypt_key set, the export is encrypted in blocks: the first line is --axonbase-backup-encrypted-v2--, followed by one Base64 line per block of up to 64 KiB. Each block uses AES-256-GCM (Advanced Encryption Standard with Galois/Counter Mode) and its own random nonce, and the authenticated data holds the block index and a last-block flag, so reordering, removing or truncating blocks is detected. The key derivation is the one used by the S3 backups. The restore recognizes the format by the header: plain files, block-encrypted files and the single-block encrypted format of the S3 backups are accepted. Restoring an encrypted file needs the same s3_encrypt_key.
backup_stream_restore_desc: The checks run in this order: confirm missing gives 400; a node in a cluster gives 409, even with force=true; storage that already has data gives 409 unless force is true. Then the server reads the whole body into a temporary file, decrypting it as it goes, and only after that touches the storage. Reading everything validates the entire stream, including the AES-GCM (Advanced Encryption Standard, Galois/Counter Mode) authentication of every block and of the last one, and the limits: a line over 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) or a body over 64 GiB gives 400. Then the header is checked. Only when all of that passes does the server erase every key of the storage in batches and apply the lines from the temporary file. So a body that is not a backup, that is truncated or altered, or that cannot be decrypted (for example with another s3_encrypt_key) answers 400 and the existing data stays intact. The temporary file is deleted at the end, and needs free space in the temporary directory about the size of the decrypted backup. The restore replaces the contents instead of merging: restoring a single incremental file leaves only the keys of that file. To rebuild from a full backup plus incrementals, use POST /admin/v1/backups/{name}/restore, which merges the chain. After a restore, including one that fails halfway, the root user is registered again with the configured credentials. The success answer is 200 with {"restored":true,"restoredKeys":N}, where N is the number of keys applied.
backup_stream_memory_desc: The export scans the storage and writes to the response as it goes, the restore reads the body line by line, and the encryption holds one block at a time, so memory does not grow with the size of the instance. BackupMemoryTest checks it: 200,000 encrypted keys of 400 bytes each (a file of about 140 MB, larger than the heap) are exported to disk and restored on RocksDB with -Xmx256m (a 256 MB heap limit for the JVM, Java Virtual Machine), without OutOfMemoryError. The test fails if the heap peak goes more than 160 MB above the starting point; a local run reported a peak of about 16 MB. It takes about 80 seconds, so it only runs with -Daxon.memtest=true.
adminapi_ex_stats_desc: GET /admin/v1/databases/{ns}/{db}/tables/{table}/stats needs the viewer role within the scope of the database and answers 404 for an unknown table. count walks the keys of the table without decoding any document, so the cost grows with the number of records; with a columnar index it counts the keys of that index instead. fields and indexes have the same shape as in the tables route. vectorFields lists the columns of the vector indexes. geoFields is the union of three sources: fields whose declared type starts with geometry or geo, or is point; columns of GEO indexes; and, only in SCHEMALESS tables, the fields found in a sample of the first 50 documents whose value is an object with a string type and a coordinates member. In a SCHEMALESS table with no GEO index, a geometry field that shows up only after those 50 documents is not detected.
security_truststore_desc: A truststore sent to POST /admin/v1/truststores is recorded in the control plane (name and file path) and is loaded again when the server restarts. DELETE /admin/v1/truststores/{name} also removes the record, so the truststore does not come back. The JKS password is never stored: after a restart the file is read without it, which loads the trusted certificates but skips the integrity check. Limitations: the file stays on the node that received the upload (next to the data directory), so the record is useless on a node that does not have the file; the collector mode and the OIDs of a truststore are not persisted, and a reloaded truststore has no collector; a truststore created with CREATE JKS in SQL is not persisted and has to be registered again after a restart. The upload is atomic: the server writes the file to a temporary name, opens it with the password and only then replaces the previous file. A new upload that is invalid (wrong password, corrupted file) answers 400 and the truststore that was already there stays as it was.
security_saga_title: CANCEL SAGA and the viewer role
security_saga_desc: A session whose role is explicitly viewer, such as a user or service token with only that role, cannot run CANCEL SAGA and gets a permission error (code -32002). Sessions with no recognized role keep working as before, because the tokens the SDKs obtain for a DATABASE scope usually carry no role and cancel their own sagas. The rule is therefore a restriction on the viewer role, not a barrier for every identity: a DATABASE user with no role, or with only a custom role such as editor, can still cancel. The management API route stays at operator.
config_conf_desc: This is the axonbase.conf.example of the repository, with every key that the server reads. The file uses key = value lines; the keys are the lowercase form of the AXON_* variables (root_user is AXON_ROOT_USER). The root user and password keys are root_user and root_password: user and pass do not exist. Keys the server does not know are ignored without an error, so a misspelled key silently leaves the default in place. Values are applied in the order default, file, AXON_* variables, CLI flags, each overriding the previous. A few settings exist only as environment variables (see the table below).
config_conf_code:
# axonbase.conf: key = value, "#" starts a comment.
# Precedence: CLI flags > AXON_* environment variables > this file > defaults.
# Each key has an AXON_<KEY IN UPPERCASE> variable (root_user -> AXON_ROOT_USER).
# Unknown keys are ignored silently: check the spelling.

# Storage: "memory" or the RocksDB directory.
path = data
bind = 127.0.0.1
port = 8000
# Plain HTTP port used when tls_cert is set (0 disables it).
# plain_port = 8080
require_auth = true
# Message language: pt-BR or en.
# lang = en

# The real keys are root_user and root_password (not "user" and "pass").
secret = change-me-signing-secret
root_user = root
root_password = change-me-root-password

# Limits and HTTP (milliseconds, except counts).
# query_timeout = 30000
# txn_timeout = 300000
# rate_limit = 0
# shutdown_timeout = 10000
# http_threads = 32
# http_queue = 100
# cors_origins = https://panel.example.com

# TLS: server PKCS12 keystore, its password, and the JKS truststore of client CAs.
# tls_cert = certs/server/server.p12
# tls_key = changeit
# tls_ca = certs/truststores/icpbrasil.jks

# Optional cluster. Leave cluster_id empty for local mode.
# cluster_id = primary
# node_id = node-1
# raft_bind = 127.0.0.1:9000
# raft_peers = 127.0.0.1:9001,127.0.0.1:9002

# Periodic S3 backup. Leave s3_bucket empty to turn it off.
# s3_encrypt_key also encrypts the /admin/v1/backups/export download.
# s3_endpoint = http://localhost:9000
# s3_bucket = axonbase
# s3_prefix = backups
# s3_access = minioadmin
# s3_secret = minioadmin
# s3_interval = 60000
# s3_encrypt_key =
# s3_retention = 10

# Operation audit and AI audit (needed by CREATE AI AUDIT).
# audit_enabled = false
# audit_user_from = auth
# audit_select = false
# audit_max_body = 65536
# ai_provider = claude
# ai_model = claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022
# ai_api_key = sk-ant-...
# ai_base_url
obs_logs_desc: Besides stdout, the server keeps the latest log lines in memory. GET /admin/v1/logs returns them (filters limit, level and since) and GET /admin/v1/logs/stream sends the new ones as an SSE (Server-Sent Events) stream; both need the viewer role. AXON_LOG_BUFFER sets how many lines are kept (default 10000), and the buffer is emptied on restart. The request format, the fields of each entry and examples are in Management API, section Logs.
search_geo_json_desc: Point, LineString and Polygon go into a document as JSON literals in the statement, with CREATE and UPDATE, and come back unchanged on SELECT. UPDATE ... SET p = {...} replaces only that field. geo::distance(a, b) (meters, between two points) and geo::contains(polygon, point) work in WHERE with a field or a JSON literal on either side. The example is the one covered by the integration test over /sql.
act_intro: See what the server is doing and act on it: statements running now, slow statements, sessions and open transactions. Everything is per node and lives in memory. AxonBase Enterprise shows it in the Activity screen; the same data is available on the management API.
act_endpoints_desc: All under /admin/v1/activity and only for ROOT-scope callers. Reading needs the viewer role; cancelling a statement and rolling back a transaction need operator; ending a session needs admin.
act_endpoints_rows: Counters for the cards: running, slow, cancelled, sessions, open transactions, version conflicts, thresholds.
Statements running now with user, database, elapsed time, origin and fingerprint.
Recent statements that passed the slow threshold, newest first.
Per-fingerprint stats: calls, errors, total, mean, p95 and max time. orderBy: total, max, count, mean, p95.
WebSocket connections and issued access tokens.
Sessions with a BEGIN still open: age, pending writes and deletes.
Version conflicts since start, total and per table.
Discards the pending writes. The session stays connected. Refused with 409 while the session is running a statement.
Closes a WebSocket (rolling back its transaction) or revokes a token. Refused for your own session and for the root user.
act_cancel_desc: Cancellation is cooperative: the executor checks a flag at every storage access, so the statement stops at its next read or write, normally within milliseconds, and the client receives the error "query cancelled". A write that already changed records before it stopped keeps those changes; use a transaction when you need all or nothing. The same flag is raised when a statement passes the query timeout, so a timed-out statement no longer keeps running in the background.
act_locks_desc: AxonBase uses optimistic concurrency. A commit is rejected when a record it read has changed in the meantime, instead of waiting on a lock. Contention therefore shows up as open transactions (they keep an old view of the data and may fail to commit) and as version conflicts, counted per table in axe_txn_conflicts_total. Idle connections, and the transactions on them, are closed after the txn_timeout setting.
act_privacy_desc: Every list carries the fingerprint: the statement with text and number values replaced by ?, so two statements that differ only in values share one. The full statement text is returned only to callers with the operator or admin role (the Axon-Role-Cap header can lower it). The slow_query log event carries the fingerprint only. With AXON_ACTIVITY_CAPTURE_SQL=false the full text is never kept.
act_config_rows: A statement running at least this long is slow. Also drives axe_query_slow_total.
How many recent slow statements are kept in memory (maximum 10000). A restart clears them.
false keeps only fingerprints and never the statement text.
act_metrics_rows: Statements stopped by a cancel or a timeout.
Open WebSocket connections (ws) and valid access tokens (token).
Commits rejected by a version conflict.
act_examples_code:
# who is running what right now (viewer)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/admin/v1/activity/queries

# slow statements grouped by shape, worst total time first
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "http://localhost:8000/admin/v1/activity/top?orderBy=total&limit=20"

# cancel a running statement (operator)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/admin/v1/activity/queries/<id>/cancel

# roll back an open transaction (operator) and end a session (admin)
curl -X POST   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/admin/v1/activity/transactions/<session>/rollback
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/admin/v1/activity/sessions/<session>
axonpl_intro: AxonPL is the programming language built into AxonBase 0.9.0. It is a small subset of Python that runs inside the server, next to the data, so a piece of business logic is stored once and called by name from a query (SQL, Structured Query Language), from a script or from an agent. This page covers the language, the limits, the channels that can call it and the debugger. The debugger has an API (Application Programming Interface) under /admin/v1. That API works over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol).

blocks.text: A function is read-only and can appear inside a query. A procedure may write and is started with CALL. A package groups constants and functions under one name and can keep state between calls.

rows: SELECT, WHERE, DEFINE FIELD ... ASSERT, RETURN
Functions read, and a package function called with CALL may write

blocks.text: The body goes between $$ delimiters. When the body itself contains $$, use a tagged delimiter such as $x$ ... $x$. Lines inside the body are numbered from 1.

items: Parameters accept a type (for example int, number or string) and a default value. Arguments are validated and converted: '5' and 5.0 become 5 for an int parameter, and 'abc' is rejected with a message naming the argument. A missing argument and too many arguments are also errors.

CREATE refuses a name that already exists. CREATE OR REPLACE swaps the program and raises its version, which INFO FOR shows together with the parameters, the return type, the docstring and the source. A name cannot change kind: a function cannot be replaced by a procedure.
Names that clash with the language are reserved, for example count, now, fn, math, string and db. A syntax error is reported when the program is created, not when it is first called.
Names that start with an underscore are private to a package and cannot be called from outside. INFO FOR PACKAGE lists the public constants and functions.

SECURITY INVOKER (the default) runs with the identity of whoever calls. SECURITY DEFINER runs with the identity of the owner, so Data Rules and permissions are those of the owner. Only an admin may create a DEFINER program.

blocks.text: This function applies a discount. It is used in the select list, in WHERE and in the ASSERT of a field, and also called directly.
Inside a program, db runs AxonQL and log writes messages. Parameters are named and written as $name in the statement. The session variables of the caller are restored when the call ends.

rows: The first row, or null when there is none
The number of rows, or the value of a single count()
The result of a statement that writes (procedures only)
Writes to the call log and to the server log

blocks.text: A function that tries to write fails with a read-only error and nothing is stored. The same statement inside a procedure works, and the procedure must be started with CALL (RETURN name() on a procedure points to CALL).

blocks.code:
CREATE PROCEDURE bom() AS $$ return db.exec("CREATE x CONTENT {a: 1}") $$;
CALL bom();

blocks.text: Every call to a procedure is atomic. Outside a transaction it runs in an implicit one; inside a BEGIN block it runs behind a savepoint. If the program raises an error, only its own writes are undone, indexes included, and the transaction of the caller stays open.

A program cannot change scope with USE and cannot control transactions with BEGIN, COMMIT or CANCEL. Schema statements (DDL, Data Definition Language) inside a program require the admin role. Data Rules and table permissions apply to every db call with the identity of the caller (or of the owner, in a DEFINER program). A viewer cannot call a procedure.

A package is a module. Top-level assignments are constants or global state, and each def is a function. Another package is imported with import, and its functions are called as name.function(). The built-in modules math, json, db and log can be imported too.

items: The import is checked when the package is created. A package that does not exist, a name that is a function and not a package, and any cycle (including a replace that closes one, reported as a -> c -> b -> a) are refused, and the original keeps working.
DROP PACKAGE lists the packages that still import the one being dropped and refuses until they are removed.
Global state lives as long as the package is loaded. CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE loads it again from the new source, so a counter starts from the new initial value.

A package that holds only immutable constants runs its functions in parallel. A package whose functions change globals (with global, or by changing a list or dictionary in place) takes a lock: calls to that package run one at a time, which keeps a counter free of lost updates under concurrent calls. Functions and procedures without package state never take that lock.

blocks.code:
CREATE PACKAGE cont AS $$
n = 0
def inc():
    global n
    n = n + 1
    return n
$$;

RETURN cont::inc();   -- 1
RETURN cont::inc();   -- 2

blocks.text: Every call runs under limits. Passing one stops the call and returns error -32041. Any other error raised by the program, such as a division by zero or a raise, returns -32040 with a traceback in Python style that shows the program lines and never Java paths.
A running call can be cancelled from the activity list, the same way as a statement. A runaway loop such as while True stops at the step limit.

Besides POST /sql, a stored program can be called by name through MCP (Model Context Protocol) and GraphQL. These two channels do not run arbitrary AxonQL, so the program is created through /sql and then called by the channel. The caller needs a role that can call it (a viewer cannot call a procedure).
A program error comes back in the channel with its code (-32040 or -32041) and the traceback.

rows: Calls that ended in a program error
Debug sessions cancelled for being idle

blocks.text: Programs are part of the database: they are replicated in a cluster, restored from a backup, included in the export and import of a database, and listed by INFO FOR DATABASE under functions, procedures and packages. A program that no longer compiles after an upgrade is marked as broken and does not stop the server from starting; replacing it fixes it. The Docker image of 0.9.0 already includes the axonbase-pl module.

A debug session runs a program on its own server thread. It stops at breakpoints and steps, and the client drives it with commands. Every line is a line of the user body: line 1 is the first line of the function or procedure body, and the header the engine adds does not count. In a package the line is the one in the package text.

items: By default the run happens in a transaction that is always rolled back, including procedures that write, on error, on stop and on idle. Inside the session the writes are visible to the program and to evaluate, but not to other connections.

commit=true confirms the transaction at the end and requires the admin role (and the leader, in a cluster). If the run fails or is stopped, nothing is committed. Without commit, schema statements inside the program are refused.

The debugger uses the identity of whoever starts it, with the same Data Rules and permissions. It needs the same level as CREATE FUNCTION: a role other than viewer and a scope that covers the database.
The AxonPL limits apply. Time spent stopped at a breakpoint does not count against the AXON_QUERY_TIMEOUT deadline.

A paused session with no command for longer than the idle time is cancelled and rolled back (state timeout). The default is 300 seconds, and the optional AXON_PL_DEBUG_IDLE (seconds, 0 turns it off) changes it.
At most 4 sessions can be active at once per server. More than that returns 429.

rows: Lists the sessions the caller can see
Stops if active, rolls back and forgets (204)

blocks.text: For a package, {name} is package::function. The request body is optional in every field.

blocks.code:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/databases/app/main/programs/grava/debug \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"args": [10], "breakpoints": [3], "stopOnEntry": true, "commit": false, "profile": false}'

items: stopOnEntry pauses at the first statement of the body. It is true by default when there are no breakpoints and no profile.
profile runs without stopping (unless there are breakpoints) and returns the trace at the end. The trace also comes back in every debug session.

blocks.text: The commands are continue, stepOver, stepInto, stepOut, pause (stops at the next statement) and stop (cancels and rolls back). The steps only work while paused; otherwise the answer is 409. stepInto enters functions of the same program and imported packages; calls made through SQL, such as fn::other(...) inside db.query, are not followed.

GET .../events?after=N&wait=MS returns the events with seq greater than N. When there are none and the session is active it waits up to wait milliseconds (at most 30000). The client repeats the call with after=next. The event types are paused, resumed, finished, error, stopped and timeout; the last four are final and carry state, committed and, on error, the error.

The state is running, paused, finished, error, stopped or timeout. A pause carries the reason (breakpoint, step or pause), the call stack with the locals of each frame, and the globals. Values are short text (up to 200 characters, three levels of nesting and 20 items per collection). After the end the state also holds result, error, committed, log (the lines of log.* and print) and profile.

evaluate runs a one-line expression in the top frame of the pause and returns its type and value, for example {"type": "int", "value": "40"}. The evaluation works on copies of the variables, so it never changes the program. It sees locals and globals and allows db.query, db.one and db.count, but never a write. Functions of the program and imported modules are not visible. A syntax or run error in the expression returns 400, and outside a pause the answer is 409.

The trace lists, per line, how many times it ran and its exclusive time in microseconds (without the time of the functions it calls and without time spent paused). It also lists every db call in order, with the SQL text, duration, rows and the program line that triggered it.

Errors use the standard format of /admin/v1: 400 (BAD_REQUEST), 401, 403 (FORBIDDEN, for example commit=true without admin), 404 (NOT_FOUND), 409 (CONFLICT, a command at the wrong time) and 429 (TOO_MANY_DEBUG_SESSIONS). An error in the debugged program is not an HTTP error: the session moves to the error state with the message and the traceback.

items: There is no pause on exception and there are no conditional breakpoints.
A session keeps the last 2000 events, and finished sessions stay 10 minutes in memory (or until DELETE).
In a cluster, a debug run without commit happens on the node that received the request and replicates nothing.

axonpl_sections.title: Using it in the Enterprise Workspace

blocks.text: AxonBase Enterprise 0.8.0 edits, runs and debugs programs in the Workspace without extra setup.

items: Program tree: inside each database the groups Functions, Procedures and Packages show the signature and version. A program that no longer compiles gets a warning icon. Double click or Enter opens the editor, and the context menu opens, copies the name or deletes the program (you confirm by typing the name). The New program button creates a function, a procedure or a package.

Editor: a signature form (name, parameters with type and default, RETURNS, INVOKER or DEFINER) above a Python editor with highlighting, line numbers, autocomplete and snippets for db.query, db.one, db.count, db.exec, log.info, loops and try. Ctrl or Cmd+S saves, as CREATE OR REPLACE for an existing program and as CREATE for a new one. A refusal from the engine appears under the editor, with the offending line underlined.

Run: a form for the arguments follows the parameters and types. Run executes RETURN for a function and CALL for a procedure (a procedure really writes). Run with profile and Debug execute in a debug session and undo the changes at the end.

Debug: click the editor margin or press F9 to set a breakpoint. The shortcuts are F8 (continue), F10 (step over), F11 (step into), Shift+F11 (step out), F6 (pause) and Shift+F5 (stop). On a pause the current line is highlighted, and the panel shows the call stack, the locals of the chosen frame, the globals and a field to evaluate expressions. A permanent notice says the changes will be undone. The Commit at the end option appears only for administrators and asks for the program name.

Timeline and heat map: after Run with profile or Debug, the Queries and profile tab lists the db queries in the order they ran (SQL, duration bar, rows and source line) and the profile by line. The Heat map button paints the editor lines by time spent, and clicking a line number jumps the editor to it.

scale_intro: Version 0.9.0 rewrites the storage and query path of a single node. No setting is required: the engine adjusts threads, caches and buffers by itself from the cores and the memory it sees. The one choice that matters is how often the write log is forced to disk, described below. The numbers on this page come from the development measurements of the project, taken in the environments described next to each table, and they are not a promise for your hardware.

blocks.text: The WAL (Write-Ahead Log) of RocksDB is always on. The optional variable AXON_STORAGE_SYNC (or the property -Daxon.storage.sync) chooses when the operating system is forced to write that log to disk with fsync.

rows: fsync in the background every 1 second

Whatever is still in the operating system cache

blocks.text: A crash of the database process alone loses nothing in any of the three modes, because the log is written before the write is acknowledged.

On macOS a full fsync (F_FULLFSYNC) costs about 19 ms, so always measures 50 operations per second with one thread and 192 with eight. On Linux the cost is usually much lower, and the table of load over HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) below shows it. Choose always when a zero-loss window is mandatory and the write rate is low.

scale_sections.title: What changed in storage and queries

items: The global storage monitor was replaced by 1024 locks by key range and lock-free iterator reads.

Value and version are written in a single atomic batch. Each write command (CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, RELATE, UNRELATE) writes the record, the indexes and the edges in one batch, so a command that fails halfway leaves no rows and no index entries.
SELECT ... LIMIT stops scanning when the limit is reached, and ORDER BY ... LIMIT uses a fixed-size heap (top-K).
The GEO index (geographic position) keeps the coordinates in the entry itself and answers the N nearest by expanding rings; EXPLAIN reports it as GEO_KNN.
Vector indexes, version counters and the audit trail have a constant cost per write. Before, every write listed the whole log.
The hot path of /sql (query fingerprint, id generation, log buffer and the JWT (JSON Web Token, the sign-in token) cache) no longer allocates or locks per request.
A DELETE now frees its UNIQUE index entry, so the same value can be written again.

backup_chain_desc: The full backup and the incrementals form a chain. To restore, send the full backup followed by the incrementals, in order, in the same body. The engine validates everything before touching the database: the first segment must be a full one, and each incremental's since must equal the version of the previous segment. An incomplete, out-of-order, tampered or truncated chain answers BACKUP_CHAIN_INVALID, BACKUP_CHECKSUM or BACKUP_TRUNCATED and the database stays intact. Restoring a lone incremental is refused. Through AxonBase Enterprise the agent builds the chain and checks each link's sha256 before sending. v1 files are still accepted, but they do not escape COLUMNAR index keys and silently lose those lines: take v1 backups of tables with that index again.
backup_chain_code:
# full, then incrementals from the watermark returned in X-Axon-Backup-Version
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/backups/export?type=full" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -D full.h -o full.axbak
WM=$(grep -i x-axon-backup-version full.h | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}')
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/backups/export?type=incremental&since=$WM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o inc1.axbak

# restore: the body is the concatenation in order
cat full.axbak inc1.axbak | curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/v1/backups/restore?confirm=true&force=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' --data-binary @-

limitations_intro: Read this page before using 1.0.0 in production. It gathers the known security limitations, the experimental features and what has not been verified yet.
limitations_warning: Do not rely on PERMISSIONS to hide data in reads by record id, FETCH, linked record reads or LIVE SELECT. The read condition is not applied on those paths. A fix is planned for 1.0.1.
limitations_security: Read PERMISSIONS do not apply to direct access by id (RETURN t:1.field), to FETCH or to the read of a linked record.

Do not offer free AxonQL queries to anyone who may not read the whole table. Enforce access in the application, or split data into databases and give each user an identity scoped to their own database.
LIVE SELECT does not apply read PERMISSIONS to notifications, and a $parameter in its filter is read from the variables of whoever writes.
Do not expose the WebSocket connection to anyone who may not read the table. A user with a data rule cannot open LIVE SELECT.
SHOW SAGA TRANSACTION shows the previous state of records to whoever reaches the saga, without read PERMISSIONS, data rules or masks.
In databases with sagas, grant access only to those who may see the data.
Whoever reaches a saga and can write can cancel it, and cancelling restores the previous state even where PERMISSIONS would deny that write.
Grant write access in those databases only to trusted identities.
$saga_corr and the X-Correlation-Id header grant no scope check, and a saga opened without a namespace and without steps can be finished by any identity that writes.
Do not accept a correlation id from the end client. Coordinate sagas with a namespace or root identity.
REEMBED does not require an administrator and rewrites rows without checking PERMISSIONS.
Do not grant writes to anyone who may not rewrite the whole table.
A DATABASE LINK is visible to the whole namespace: a database user can query it with the credential stored in the link.
Use a minimal credential in the link and do not create it in a namespace with restricted users.
In a database.table query by a namespace or root identity, the PERMISSIONS and data rules of the session database apply.
For users subject to rules, use a database scoped identity.
A viewer still stores a table definition by querying a table that does not exist.
Review the catalog regularly with INFO FOR DATABASE.
Data rules are not a complete isolation boundary: masks do not reach nested fields, WHERE and ORDER BY allow inferring the value, and the EXPLAIN estimate counts hidden rows.
Read the coverage and limits on the Data Rules page before relying on them.
In AI Audit, AUDITED BY assigned after login only applies at the next login, and two audited operators can approve each other's WARNING cases.
Assign the audit before granting access.
Through the Enterprise panel, an audited operator can decide their own case.
Do not give the operator role in the panel to audited people.
The Raft port has no authentication or encryption.
Expose it only on a private network.
Without TLS between the gateway and the shards, the shard secret travels in clear text.
Use TLS or a private network.
limitations_experimental_intro: They pass the functional tests, but their load and failure targets were not measured on separate machines. Behavior and storage format may change in a 1.x release. Test with your own load and keep backups.
limitations_experimental: Multiple shards (SHARD BY, gateway and shard backup)

limitations_other: In JOIN, a filter on the joined table may empty the result, ORDER BY is ignored and LEFT JOIN behaves as an inner join.
A query with AT returns the current value when there is no history for the requested instant.
GraphQL ignores the requested fields, the arguments and the other query roots.
CANCEL SAGA does not undo a write on a record whose key is a typed value, a list or an object: it returns an error and the saga stays in COMPENSATING.
BEGIN SAGA with an undefined name is accepted, with no participants.
The published Spring Data package has no repositories, template or annotations.
Writing new records on a single node became about 12% slower with 1 thread and 6% with 8 threads, compared with 0.10.1.
The load and resilience gates on dedicated machines did not run on the code of this release, and disaster recovery was never tested against a real S3 store.
